evidence: Receiving online DO2 sensor, t=47.8 h: 10.58 mg/L; t=48.0 h: 3.20 mg/L — abrupt ~7.4 mg/L step drop indicating a sudden OUR event
Receiving DO2 t=49.5–52.0 h: slow decline, linear fit slope −0.19 mg/L/h; final value 2.31 mg/L at t=52 h, only 0.31 mg/L above the 2 mg/L hard limit
Linear projection under KEEP: DO ≈1.54 mg/L at +4 h, ≈0.76 mg/L at +8 h — centrally predicted violation of the post-decision DO ≥ 2 mg/L constraint

Receiving delayed product assay (available t=52 h, sampled t=47.8 h): P = 2.61 g/L and rising — production ongoing, so stop (zero counted production) and strong 40% feed cuts impose avoidable mass loss

Source batches (source-1..3) show the same DO event at ~48 h recovering with air/feed manipulation, supporting that a bounded air/feed intervention can re-establish DO margin; no physics model tool was available, so this is a coarse, source-calibrated-by-analogy estimate, not a calibrated prediction
submission.rationale: At the 52 h decision point the receiving fermenter shows an abrupt oxygen-demand event: DO2 fell from ~10.6 to ~3.2 mg/L at t=48 h and continues drifting down at ~0.19 mg/L/h, now at 2.31 mg/L. KEEP is centrally predicted to violate the hard 2 mg/L DO limit within ~1-2 h, so no-intervention is infeasible. increase_air alone (+15% OTR) leaves thin margin against the observed persistent OUR drift and forecast error; strong_feed_reduction (-40% feed) over-sacrifices product mass relative to the modest deficit. combined (-20% feed, +15% air) reduces oxygen uptake and raises transfer simultaneously, closing the predicted deficit with margin on both mechanisms while retaining most product-forming capacity. Product was 2.61 g/L at the last assay and rising, so preserving production matters; stop is unnecessary because a bounded, evidence-supported feasible plan exists. No physics model tool was available, so this relies on the observed DO trajectory and bounded intervention ranges.
submission.uncertainty: No calibrated physics model was available; the DO projection is a linear extrapolation of a 2.5 h window and could over- or understate the true OUR trajectory. If OUR continues growing (e.g., contamination-like dynamics), even the combined action might not hold DO ≥ 2 mg/L at every future time, in which case strong_feed_reduction or stop would be the fallback. Conversely, if the event is transient, combined retains more product than strong_feed_reduction. The +15% air cap is assumed to translate into ~15% higher transfer; actual OTR gain depends on hidden kLa and saturation parameters of the receiving process, which differ from the source.
